summary: Spike in 5xx errors after large embedding batch where inconsistent HTTP/2 window settings caused ingress stalls and upstream terminations
description:
Issue summary:
We observed a sustained elevation in 5xx error rate (502/503) for customer ParcelFlow starting 2026-03-10 02:45 UTC, coinciding with a large embedding bulk upload + client library that negotiated non-default HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE behavior. Impact: degraded request success for embedding requests and some downstream generation calls routed to the same tenant pool.

Impact:
- ~18% increase in 5xx rate for the tenant over a 40-minute window (approx 02:45-03:25 UTC).
- Customer reports failed batch uploads and timeouts; impact on production pipelines for ParcelFlow.
- No full platform outage but several upstreams entered unhealthy and triggered fallback routing which increased latency for other tenants briefly.

Environment:
- prod us-west; ingress fleet behind apigw-cluster-7; serving-runtimes pinned to embedder-xlarge-v2; customer on enterprise plan with dedicated-shard affinity.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer initiated a large embedding upload (multipart, ~4k items, variable chunk sizes) at 02:38 UTC.
2) The client library negotiated HTTP/2 settings including smaller initial window and aggressive WINDOW_UPDATE pacing (non-default).
3) Ingress accepted connections but observed slow downstream write progress; keepalive probes delayed; ingress healthchecks flagged several upstream runtimes as unhealthy.
4) Serving runtimes accumulated inflight streams, thread pool growth, and eventually a few runtime workers hit memory pressure and restarted, producing 502/503 responses.

Observed logs & metrics (high level):
- apigw-7 logs: repeated 408/stream-timeout entries followed by 502 upstream errors.
- ingress-proxy metrics: write_latency_p50 -> spike from 12ms to 520ms; http2_active_streams per connection -> sustained >250 on impacted sockets.
- serving-runtime: thread_pool_queue_length grew from baseline 40 to 700; OOM-like memory pressure logs before clean restarts.
- kv-cache: high eviction churn due to concurrent embedding warmups.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- 02:53 UTC: Support placed temporary rate-limit on the customer's bulk embedding route (soft-cap) to prevent further burst writes.
- 03:00 UTC: Infra team cycled a subset of ingress nodes with experimental http2 window normalization patch (see PR) to clamp client-advertised window to safe bounds.
- 03:12 UTC: Gradual drain + restart of the hottest serving runtimes and increased keepalive timeout thresholds to reduce false unhealthy markings.

Customer-facing message prepared:
- A message acknowledging elevated error rates during bulk embedding uploads, a short-term mitigation (rate limiting), and ETA for full remediation. Posted to #support-parcelflow.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses tested:
- Hypothesis 1: Model hot-swap or quantization fallback caused sudden OOMs — checked model lifecycle logs; no hot-swap during window. (DISPROVED)
- Hypothesis 2: Tenant-level prefetch/kv-cache invalidations thrashing runtime memory — cache eviction rate correlated with spike but was secondary. (PARTIAL)
- Hypothesis 3: Client HTTP/2 SETTINGS mismatch created head-of-line stalls, causing ingress to keep many streams open and starving runtime thread pools — confirmed by tcpdump and http2 SETTINGS frames showing non-standard WINDOW_SIZE and delayed WINDOW_UPDATE frames. (CONFIRMED)

Key artifacts:
- tcpdump trace (trimmed) showing client pauses between WINDOW_UPDATE frames and large stream concurrency per connection (attached to ticket).
- ingress metrics and Grafana dashboard snapshots (links in comment).
- runtime crash logs showing memory pressure prior to restart (no full core dump).

Temporary workarounds considered and their tradeoffs:
1) Immediate hard rate-limit on customer (implemented soft-cap first) — prevents recurrence but degrades throughput for their pipelines.
2) Enforce http2 window clamping at ingress to normalize client behavior (low customer impact) — selected as preferred short-term and applied to a subset of nodes.
3) Increase runtime threadpool capacity for tenant shards temporarily — reduces head-of-line effects but risks cross-tenant noisy neighbor; avoided for now.

Next investigative steps planned:
- Capture full pcap for a sample connection and replay in test cluster with instrumented bookkeeping to reproduce resource amplification.
- Add synthetic test that simulates WINDOW_UPDATE stalls against ingress to validate mitigation.
- Evaluate making window-clamping a global safety feature with a config toggle per tenant.
resolution:
Partial mitigation applied: ingress window-clamping rolled to a subset of nodes and customer soft rate-limit reduced burst to safe levels. Serving runtimes were restarted and memory pressure subsided. Error rate returned to baseline by 03:40 UTC.

Permanent fix plan (in progress):
- Short term (2-3 days): finish safe-window-clamp rollout to all ingress nodes behind a feature flag; add an alert for sustained http2_active_streams per connection.
- Mid term (2 weeks): add a per-route ingest guard that detects abnormal WINDOW_UPDATE patterns and applies automatic soft-throttles before upstreams become unhealthy.
- Long term (1-2 months): integrate client behavior detection into the traffic routing layer and document recommended client-side settings for bulk embedding uploads.

Follow-ups assigned:
- ENG-RT: implement global safe-window-clamp feature flag (owner: Maya Chen).
- DX: produce updated embedding best-practices doc for customers (owner: Priya Nair).
- SRE: add runbook entry for http2-window-induced upstream pressure (owner: Marcus Lee).
